title: The benefits of Code Connect in the Figma MCP server
excerpt: Figma measured what happens when agents get production component context through Code Connect in the Figma MCP server: fewer tokens burned and materially better generated code. A concrete argument for wiring design systems into the agent pipeline rather than letting agents guess.
rationale: First-party measurements, not opinion: shows exactly what a design system wired into MCP buys you in agent output quality — a setup task a team can do tomorrow.

title: Introducing the new v0 API
excerpt: Vercel shipped a new v0 API, exposing its prompt-to-UI generation model programmatically so teams can build design-to-code generation into their own tools and pipelines.
rationale: A dated platform release that moves prompt-to-UI out of a chat product and into design teams' own tooling — the highest-leverage new capability in the pool.

title: Material Creator will be a true alternative to Substance 3D Designer
excerpt: World Creator developer BiteTheBytes previewed Material Creator, a node-based material authoring tool for games and VFX pitched as a real alternative to Adobe's Substance 3D Designer.
rationale: A credible new challenger in node-based material authoring — the first real alternative to a tool most 3D/product visualisation pipelines are locked into.

title: Chat is the wrong interface for AI
excerpt: An argument that the chat box is a lazy default for AI products, and that designers need interface patterns that expose model capability instead of hiding it behind a text field.
rationale: Directly attacks the default every AI product ships with, and gives designers alternative patterns to reach for on the next AI feature.

title: Show the agent's evidence before asking for one-click approval
excerpt: An agentic-UX pattern argument: never put a one-click Approve button in front of a user without first surfacing the agent's evidence, diffs and reasoning trail.
rationale: A copyable approval-UI pattern for agentic products — concrete guidance on what to render beside the Approve button, which almost every agent surface gets wrong.
